Does the program only works for human - with 22 chromsomes (excluding XY)? How about other species? for example, crop plant barley that only has 7 chromsomes? Or can I simply make one single ld file that contains all chromosomes (whether it is 22 or 7, or any other number?)

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: non-human species
parts:
Hi Tianhua, 

The ldsc function is currently set-up to work for human populations with respect to assumptions about LD structure and overall selection. In general, you would not be able to do cross-species models (e.g., different types of plant barley) because the LD structures would presumably change across the different types of plants. If you are working within a single species and have LD-scores for that population than the program can be used with non-human populations. With that said you would want to put some careful thought into some of the assumptions of the model and ideally run some simulations or use a trait for which you know what the SNP heritability (h2) should be to see that you are getting numbers close the expected value. The original developers of ld-score regression have also responded to similar questions on their google group (links to those responses below). 

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/ldsc_users/cUVUcJifhSU/0EhqROm7gJgJ;context-place=msg/ldsc_users/Nag-yNFm1Mo/NWVgM6JSBQAJ

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/ldsc_users/Nag-yNFm1Mo/NWVgM6JSBQAJ

-Andrew

messages.author: 3b39745f73eec779
messages.subject: Re: non-human species
parts:
Hi,

I made an argument called "chr" for the ldsc() fuction, it defaults to 22 (most genomicSEM users study humans), but you can set it to a different value.

First reinstall genomicSEM and reboot R and then your good to go, use the new argument like like this:

# for 7 chromosomes: 
ldsc.output <- ldsc( ... , chr=7)

Incredibly curious whether this will work, hope this helps you get on your way.

Best,
Michel

Dear Michel

I had another go using your new code after re-stall Genomic SEM, but it still asked for 22 files.

While investigating your new code, I can see that you amended the code in the line under #### READ LD SCORES - and the program was satisfied with the number of files defined by the number of chromosomes.

While there are still two places under ### READ weights, and ### READ M, respectively, the program attempts to read 22 files.

It would be appreciated very much if you could assist here again

Thank you very much
Tianhua
